newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia bank union seeks assurances on jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia bank union seeks assurances on jobs.

text.p: The Finance Sector Union (FSU) said on Monday it wanted St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Ltd to commit to no forced redundancies and to consulting with the union on any changes in their proposed merger.

"We are calling on St George and Advance to make a public commitment to job security, no forced retrenchments, adequate redeployment opportunities and a real consultative process with the union on any changes," said Tony Beck, the FSU Joint National Secretary.
Beck said in a statement that the union intended to take an active and resolute position on the proposed merger.

Earlier, St George announced it would bid an effective A$7.30 per share for Advance, including A$2.10 in cash, a 20 cent special cash dividend and new St George shares up to a value of A$5.00 per Advance Bank share.
The merger plan values Advance at A$2.65 billion.

St George Managing Director Jim Sweeney told a news conference announcing the merger that up to 1,000 workers could be laid off as the merged banks rationalised the 167 branches and other operations where the two banks overlapped.
Sweeney had also said the banks had consulted with the unions about the merger and they were confident the rationalisations would take place with a minimum of disruption.
The FSU said it had received hundreds of calls from workers concerned about their future.
The FSU said it would "not sit back and let the merged entity slash jobs and branch networks at the expense of staff and customers."
